gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's '4,800 W lifting' / '3,900 W Power Lifting' and EcoFlow's '2,200 W X-Boost' headline numbers are resistive-only modes that do not count toward starting a furnace blower motor, and that BLUETTI's Elite 300 and Elite 200 V2 US pages publish no true surge rating at all, while EcoFlow, Jackery and ALLPOWERS publish surge and boost as separate numbers.
standout_why: Outage Authority (cited) lists Jackery 1000 v2 '1,500 W continuous, 3,000 W surge' and notes 'no surge rating given' for the AC180 and only 'total AC output' for the Elite 200 v2, but never explains why BLUETTI has no surge number or that its Power Lifting figure is resistive-only; it gives no furnace start-up figure. PreparedStates gives a DTE starting factor of 3 (1,350–1,800 W) but names no models. The Reliance TF instructions (cited) are about the switch, not the inverter. Neither rival mentions X-Boost or Power Lifting at all.
decides: A PSC blower needs roughly 1,350–1,800 W to start (PreparedStates quoting DTE), so for 2,400 W-and-up stations (Elite 300, Elite 200 V2, DELTA 3 Max Plus, R4000) the continuous rating alone covers the start and the missing or resistive-only boost number changes nothing; it confirms the 2,400 W+ picks. For 1,800 W-class units (AC180, Elite 100 V2, DELTA 3 Plus) the shopper must not read 'Power Lifting 2,700 W' or 'X-Boost 2,200 W' as surge headroom; only a published true surge (Jackery 1000 v2 3,000 W per Outage Authority; DELTA 3 Plus not confirmed on the maker page today) counts, which keeps the AC180's 'PSC start unverified' flag and argues for the EcoFlow/Jackery units in that class.

findings.label: AC continuous / boost wording / UPS / price
findings.value: 2,400 W continuous; '4,800 W lifting'; 10 ms UPS; US$1,199
findings.note: Page wording: '2,400 W output (4,800 W lifting) for heavy loads like microwaves and heaters.' No 'surge' or 'peak' figure and no duration is stated anywhere on the page. In-box list includes a grounding screw; no bonding or furnace guidance.

findings.label: AC continuous / Power Lifting wording / price
findings.value: 2,600 W (120 V, 21.6 A); 'kick into 3900W Power Lifting mode for pure resistive loads'; US$899
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Portable Power Station
findings.note: BLUETTI itself limits the 3,900 W figure to 'pure resistive loads'. No surge/peak rating is published; the UPS FAQ entry has no answer shown. For a blower motor the comparable number is therefore 2,600 W continuous, not 3,900 W.

findings.label: AC continuous / boost wording / status
findings.note: No duration and no statement whether Turbo Boost is a surge or a resistive-only mode. The page says '24/7 UPS' with no ms figure. The store marks the base unit Discontinued.

findings.label: X-Boost wording (maker store)
findings.value: 'With X-Boost mode get up to 2200W output power to run 99% of home appliances'; bundle with 220 W panel US$919
findings.note: Read via storecheck on us.ecoflow.com; the standalone DELTA 3 Plus page returned HTTP 429 three times today, so its continuous and surge figures are not confirmed from the maker page in this pass. The 2,200 W X-Boost figure is the one EcoFlow leads with; it is not the surge rating.

findings.label: Continuous / surge / X-Boost stated as three separate numbers
findings.value: 3,000 W continuous; 6,000 W surge; X-Boost 'up to 3800W'; 10 ms auto-switch; US$1,149
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus Portable Power Station (2048Wh)
findings.note: EcoFlow's own page separates '6000W surge output' from 'X-Boost mode ... up to 3800W', so surge and boost are different quantities. Same page: DELTA 3 Max (non-Plus) 2,400 W / 4,800 W surge / X-Boost 3,400 W, US$879.

findings.label: Continuous / surge / X-Boost / switchover
findings.value: 3,600 W continuous; 7,200 W surge; X-Boost up to 4,600 W; 10 ms auto-switch; US$1,599
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra Plus Portable Power Station (3072Wh)
findings.note: Page also lists '2 Easy Ways to Connect to Your Home: Manual Transfer Switch and Inlet Box'.

findings.label: Continuous / surge / switchover
findings.value: 2,200 W continuous; 4,400 W surge; switchover under 20 ms; US$999 (pre-order, ships Nov 16)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 Portable Power Station
findings.note: Read via storecheck. Jackery publishes a plain surge number with no boost mode. Same store today: Explorer 1500 v2 2,000 W / 4,000 W surge US$849; HomePower 1000 v2 1,500 W, sub-10 ms, US$549; HomePower 1000 Plus v2 1,800 W / 3,600 W peak, <10 ms, US$669.

findings.label: Continuous / surge / availability
findings.value: '4000W (6000W surge) Pure Sine Wave AC Output'; UPS stated without ms; US$1,499, not available
findings.note: Kit pages on the same store say '3600W/4000W AC Pure Sine Wave Output (6,000W Surge)', so the continuous figure is stated two ways by the maker; the US listing's 'available: false' today.

findings.label: Furnace start-up load (rival page, for sizing the surge column)
findings.value: 450 W (1/3 hp) or 600 W (1/2 hp) running; starting factor 3 gives about 1,350–1,800 W
findings.source_title: Can a Power Station Run a Gas Furnace? — PreparedStates
findings.note: PreparedStates attributes the running watts and starting factor to DTE Energy. Not a maker figure; used only to set the threshold the normalised surge column must clear.

findings.label: Furnace component loads (rival page)
findings.value: PSC blower 490 W, ECM blower 284 W, inducer 75 W, hot-surface igniter 400 W for about 37 s; about 565 W (PSC) / 359 W (ECM) with burner on
findings.source_title: Can a Power Station Run Your Gas Furnace in an Outage? | Outage Authority
findings.note: Outage Authority attributes these to an LBNL model and an NRC measurement and gives no start-up figure. It also states that the manuals it read for Jackery, Bluetti and Anker do not state neutral-ground bonding.

findings.label: Power Lifting mechanism (BLUETTI user community, not a maker spec)
findings.value: Forum reply: mode acts like a constant-current source with reduced voltage for resistive loads; a motor draws more current at low voltage
findings.note: Reached only via search summary, not opened as a page; treat as a pointer. The maker-stated fact used in the table is the Elite 200 V2 page's 'pure resistive loads' wording, not this thread.
